subject: mathematics
question_text: In a △ABC, if r₁ = 8, r₂ = 12 and r₃ = 24, then find a, b and c.

mark_split.label: Find r from the three ex-radii
Find each side from its ex-radius

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each standard result you use and the order you use them in.

steps.label: Find r from the three ex-radii
steps.margin_note: Two of the eight marks. The three ex-radii determine the in-radius through 1/r = 1/r₁ + 1/r₂ + 1/r₃ — one of the standard results, quoted rather than derived.
steps.memory_tip: 1/r = 1/r₁ + 1/r₂ + 1/r₃ — a standard result, quoted rather than derived.

recall.must_convey: That 1/r = 1/r₁ + 1/r₂ + 1/r₃ is used to find r = 4.
accept: use one over r equals the sum of the reciprocals of the three ex radii to get r equals four
the reciprocal formula gives r as four
add the reciprocals of r one r two r three to get one over r
one by r equals one by r one plus one by r two plus one by r three, r equals four
find the in radius first, it is four

steps.why: Nothing else in the chain can start without r. That single standard result is what unlocks Δ, then s, then the sides.
common_mistakes: Adding r₁ + r₂ + r₃ directly instead of their reciprocals.
Forgetting to invert at the end, giving r = 1/4.

steps.label: Find Δ and s
steps.margin_note: Two more marks. Δ = √(r r₁ r₂ r₃) is the standard result that turns four radii into an area; then s = Δ/r follows from r = Δ/s.
steps.memory_tip: Δ = √(r r₁ r₂ r₃) turns four radii into an area; then s = Δ/r follows from r = Δ/s.
lines: We know Δ = √(r r₁ r₂ r₃)

recall.must_convey: That Δ = √(r r₁ r₂ r₃) = 96 and s = Δ/r = 24.
accept: delta is the square root of r times r one r two r three which is ninety six and s is delta over r which is twenty four
the area is ninety six and the semi perimeter is twenty four
use delta equals root of the product of all four radii
delta root r r1 r2 r3 equals ninety six, s equals twenty four
find the area then the semi perimeter

steps.why: Grouping the product as 3²×4²×8² is what makes the root come out whole. Multiplying it out to 9216 first works but wastes time.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the four radii out before factorising.
Using s = rΔ instead of Δ/r.

steps.label: Find each side from its ex-radius
steps.margin_note: Three marks. Each ex-radius names one side: r₁ = Δ/(s−a) gives s−a, and s is known — so a follows. Same for b and c.
steps.memory_tip: Each ex-radius names ONE side: r₁ gives s − a, and s is known, so a follows.

recall.must_convey: That each side comes from its own ex-radius via r₁ = Δ/(s−a), giving a = 12, b = 16, c = 20.
accept: each ex radius gives its own side, s minus a is delta over r one and so on, giving twelve sixteen and twenty
use r one equals delta over s minus a to find a, similarly for b and c
the three sides are twelve sixteen and twenty
prathi ex radius oka side isthundi, a twelve b sixteen c twenty
find s minus a, s minus b, s minus c then the sides

steps.why: The subscript on the ex-radius tells you which side it belongs to: r₁ pairs with a, r₂ with b, r₃ with c. That pairing is the whole bookkeeping of the question.
common_mistakes: Pairing r₁ with b or c.
Computing s − a and reporting it as a.

steps.label: State the sides
steps.margin_note: Last mark. A quick check worth doing: a + b + c should be 2s, and 12 + 16 + 20 = 48 = 2 × 24.

recall.must_convey: That the three sides are a = 12, b = 16, c = 20.
accept: the sides are twelve sixteen and twenty
a is twelve b is sixteen c is twenty
state the three sides
a twelve, b sixteen, c twenty
the answer is twelve sixteen twenty

steps.why: a + b + c = 2s is a free check that costs one line and catches any slip in the previous step.
common_mistakes: Reporting s − a values as the sides.
Skipping the check and missing an arithmetic error.
